summary: Remove Object From Array: removes an object, referenced by its id, from a shared array when Do fires.
description: When `remove` (Do) fires, resolves `collectionId` (Array Id) to the shared array and `modifyId` (Object Id) to the shared object, removes that object from the array, and reports one outcome: `done` (Done) when the object was removed, or `unchanged` (Unchanged) when it was not in this array. An Object Id naming a record nothing has loaded is `failure` (Failure) instead — that removal is impossible rather than redundant — as is an unset id. `completed` (Completed) fires after all three. Only the array membership changes — the object itself continues to exist and can still be reached by its id. Every Array node and Repeater bound to the same Array Id updates immediately.
whenToUse: Per-item delete actions in local lists. Inside a Repeater's item component, feed `modifyId` from Repeater Item's `itemId` — that is the idiomatic 'remove this row'. For clearing everything use Clear Array; for cloud records use Delete Record.

ports.remove: Signal input (Do); performs the removal after other inputs have settled.
ports.collectionId: Value input: id of the shared array to remove from.
ports.modifyId: Connection-only value input: the id of the object to remove — inside a repeater item, wire Repeater Item `itemId` here.
ports.done: Signal (Done); fires after the object has been removed.
ports.unchanged: Signal (Unchanged); fires when the object was not in this array, so nothing was removed.
ports.failure: Signal (Failure); fires when the array or the object could not be resolved. `error` carries the reason.
ports.completed: Signal (Completed); fires after every Do whatever the outcome.

patterns: Repeater Item `itemId` → `modifyId`, delete button `onClick` → `remove`, with the list's Array Id on `collectionId`: a per-row delete button.
